looks_like_me_why: Some pages do look like me. The old bearded fellow with the bald head is close on pages 1, 4, 9, 10, 12 and 16. But it's cartooned and smoothed out. Other pages show a young boy as Jack (pages 2, 3, 14, 15). That inconsistency makes it feel less like my picture and more like a mixed mash.
rings_true_why: Story follows the old Jack and the Beanstalk lines, even the Fee-fi-fo-fum bit, so it's recognizable. But the pictures are very cinematic and sometimes don't match the text or each other. For a real children's book it feels a bit uneven.
professional_why: Artwork is high quality and polished. Colors, composition and detail look like a professional animation still. My only holdback is the inconsistent character age and a few odd choices (beans look like candy).
not_good: Inconsistent hero age — sometimes I'm the old man, sometimes Jack is a young boy (pages 2,3,14,15 vs pages 1,4,9,10,12,16). Beans look like jellybeans on pages 6–7. Some images and text don't line up perfectly. The harp being a little person (page 16) feels odd and out of tone.
liked: Nice colors and clear pictures. The cow, hen and harp look good for grandkids. The classic lines are there, and the big beanstalk/castle shots are nice.
